findings: Selection: draw only from Salesforce LAMP/Writing Alignment expert-edited literary paragraph pairs that carry an original, an expert revision, and expert-intended edit-category tags (e.g., diction/voice, imagery, clarity/coherence, pacing, grammar/mechanics, figurative control). Keep English literary paragraphs of comparable length; drop pairs with missing category tags, wholesale topic changes, or multi-paragraph scope creep. Stratify the sealed pool by primary intended category, secondary multi-label vs single-label, and edit magnitude (token/Levenshtein tertiles) so large rewrites cannot dominate. Exclude any pair with documented or probable exposure to HBQ training, prompt-tuning, or threshold calibration (ID match, near-duplicate n-gram/embedding overlap). Do not add new human raters, new rewrite sources, or extra public writing benches.

Train/holdout separation: treat HBQ as frozen. Partition LAMP/Writing Alignment into (a) contaminated/exposed IDs, permanently ineligible; (b) a small sealed holdout used once for this question; (c) unused remainder that is not a tuning set. Freeze pair IDs, preprocessing, and metric code before scoring. No iterative prompt or scorer tweaks on holdout outcomes. Publish only hashed IDs plus aggregates; never raw literary text. Separation is pair-level (original and its expert edit travel together) and, if multiple edits share a source, cluster-level so leakage cannot occur via sibling revisions.

Directionality metrics (primary question): paired lift Δs = s(expert) − s(original); pairwise win rate P(s(expert) > s(original)) with ties reported, not hidden; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank and bootstrap CIs clustered on source paragraph. Category-conditional win rates and median Δs on the intended primary tag; pre-register that lift should be larger on the intended category than on the pooled complementary tags. Magnitude-normalized lift Δs / edit_distance (and / changed-span count) so verbosity or rewrite volume is not rewarded. If HBQ is multi-head, evaluate the head that matches the intended tag as primary and the scalar/overall head as co-primary. Optional monotonicity check only when a source has multiple expert strengths: stronger intended edit should not rank below weaker.

Collateral-regression and churn (negative controls, no new humans): from each holdout original, build matched-magnitude churn variants by program only—synonym/function-word swaps, punctuation/whitespace, sentence permute that preserves clauses, and meaning-preserving paraphrase templates—never expert or crowd rewrites. Require P(s(churn) > s(original)) ≲ 0.5 and median Δs_churn ≤ 0 (pre-registered non-inferiority/null band). Untouched-dimension regression: on pairs tagged as targeting C only, Δ on non-C heads (or on complementary category slices) must not be significantly negative; report collateral-drop rate P(min_{d∉C} Δ_d < 0). Unchanged-span stability: if span or sentence scores exist, unmarked sentences should not move outside a small pre-set band. Joint success rule: expert win on intended C AND no significant churn preference AND no significant non-C drop.

Smallest useful sample: not a lab matrix and not a full dump. Pre-register one primary family (overall expert-vs-original directionality) and three secondary families (intended-category lift, churn non-preference, untouched-dimension non-regression). Smallest claimable overall directionality: n≈40 independent source paragraphs (≈80 texts). Category-conditional claims: ≥8–12 sources per primary tag, 4–6 tags → n≈48–72 sources. Joint claim including churn + collateral: n≈60–80 sources plus 1–2 churn variants per source (synthetic). Power target: 80% to detect win rate 0.65 vs 0.50 at α=0.05 one-sided on the primary, with Holm or pre-specified hierarchy on secondaries. Do not expand n to chase significance after unblinding. If a stratum has <8 sources, report descriptively and do not claim that category.

Admissible claims: at this frozen HBQ checkpoint, on this sealed literary-paragraph holdout, expert edits are scored above originals, with larger lift on annotated intended categories than on non-targeted dimensions, and matched-magnitude churn is not preferred. Inadmissible claims: general writing quality, open-domain preference, usefulness as an RL reward, ranking among systems, cross-benchmark superiority, or recovery of full expert editorial policy. Scope locks: English literary paragraphs, this expert pool, this edit ontology, this checkpoint. Output is a sealed memo of aggregates, CIs, and stratum sizes—not a leaderboard and not a benchmark-lab matrix.
recommendations: Pre-register the ID list, contamination audit, metric hierarchy, churn generators, and joint success rule; score once on frozen HBQ; lock code and temperature/decoding if scoring is model-mediated.
Report a four-cell sealed summary only: overall win rate + Δs; intended-category Δs vs complementary; churn win rate + Δs; collateral-drop rate—each with clustered CIs and n per stratum.
Use hashed pair IDs and edit-magnitude bins in any external note; never quote, paraphrase at length, or release originals/edits.
If contamination cannot be ruled out for a tag, drop that tag from confirmatory claims rather than widening the corpus.
Treat failure on churn or collateral as a veto on “quality improved” language even if expert win rate is high; that pattern is rewrite-volume bias, not alignment with expert edits.
Keep the study one-resource, one-checkpoint, one-question; refuse add-on benches, new raters, and multi-model matrices that would unseal or un-sparsify the design.
risks: Undetected LAMP/HBQ overlap would inflate expert wins and falsely certify a frozen scorer.
Sparse per-tag n makes category-conditional claims fragile; one long rewrite stratum can drive overall Δs.
Scalar-only HBQ cannot truly isolate untouched dimensions; complementary-slice and churn proxies may miss real collateral harm.
Synthetic churn may be off-manifold relative to expert edits, making “no reward for churn” either too easy or unfairly hard.
Edit-distance normalization can hide good large edits or excuse tiny noisy score jitter.
Sealed-text constraint blocks qualitative error analysis except via tags and magnitude bins, so failure modes stay under-specified.
Multiple secondary tests without a locked hierarchy will produce story-like category wins that do not replicate.
output.summary: A sealed, sparse paired test on unused Salesforce LAMP/Writing Alignment expert-edited literary paragraphs can answer whether frozen HBQ prefers those expert edits—especially on annotated intended categories—without preferring matched-magnitude churn or dropping untouched dimensions. Use a contamination-audited, stratified holdout of about 60–80 source paragraphs (40 minimum for overall directionality; 8–12 per tag for category claims), score each original vs expert once, and judge success by clustered directional lift plus explicit churn and collateral vetoes. No new humans, no raw-text release, no extra-benchmark matrix; claims stay scoped to this checkpoint, this literary edit ontology, and this sealed ID list.
